nom: Lecture 5 (part 2) — The Celtic Fringe: Northern Ireland
cartes: The Act for the Union of Great Britain and Ireland comes into force
Easter Rising (Connolly and Pearse) violently repressed: 6 days, about 370 dead, 15 leaders hanged
Éamon de Valera is elected president of Sinn Féin
Anglo-Irish Treaty: Irish Free State (26 counties) and Northern Ireland (6 counties)
Irish Civil War: victory of the pro-treaty party, partition accepted
Northern Irish parliament elected: 40 Unionists, 6 Nationalists, 6 Sinn Féin
The "Special Powers Act" gives the RUC extra powers
Creation of NICRA (Northern Ireland Civil Rights Association)
First NICRA civil rights demonstrations (beginning of the Troubles)
Bloody Sunday in Derry: British paratroopers shoot dead 13 men
The Widgery report finds no fault on the part of the soldiers
Stormont is suspended and Direct Rule from London is implemented
An agreement acceptable to all is reached after about 30 years
The "Shankill Butchers" (UVF loyalist paramilitaries) are active
Beginning of the "dirty protest" in the H-blocks
IRA prisoners begin a hunger strike campaign in the Maze prison
Bobby Sands, IRA leader, starts a hunger strike, soon followed by 15 others
Bobby Sands dies (as well as 9 others)
Tony Blair announces a new inquiry on Bloody Sunday (Lord Saville)
The Saville report is published: the civilians were unarmed, the soldiers lied
David Cameron's formal state apology for the killing of 14 marchers on Bloody Sunday
The Good Friday Agreement (Belfast Agreement) is signed
Power-sharing at Stormont: Ian Paisley (DUP) First Minister, Martin McGuinness (Sinn Féin) Deputy
Sinn Féin wins the Assembly elections (27 seats v. 25 for the DUP); Michelle O'Neill First Minister
Michelle O'Neill's campaign focuses on the cost of living and health care rather than unification
Census: 45.7% Catholic, 43.5% Protestant (more Catholics for the first time in 101 years)
"Celtic alliance": Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland jointly demand a vote on dissolving the UK (Cardiff)
Simon Jenkins' article in The Guardian on the Celtic alliance
